traceability.evidence:
Key implementation and verification artifacts for Story docs/stories/021.0-DEV-TEST-ANNOTATION-AUTO-FIX.story.md:
1) Story file - docs/stories/021.0-DEV-TEST-ANNOTATION-AUTO-FIX.story.md - Exists and matches the content provided in the prompt (verified via read_file).
2) Core rule implementation - File: src/rules/require-test-traceability.ts - Exposes ESLint rule `traceability/require-test-traceability`. - meta.fixable: "code" – integrates with ESLint --fix. - Options schema includes: - autoFixTestTemplate (boolean, default true) - autoFixTestPrefixFormat (boolean, default true) - testSupportsTemplate (string, optional) - create(context): - Determines test files via determineIsTestFile(filename, testFilePatterns). - Invokes ensureFileSupportsAnnotation(context, sourceCode, { autoFixTestTemplate, testSupportsTemplate }). - Sets up CallExpression visitor via handleCallExpression(context, { sourceCode, describeRegex, requireDescribeStory, requireTestReqPrefix, autoFixTestPrefixFormat }). - Traceability annotations explicitly bind this rule to the story and requirements: - "@supports docs/stories/021.0-DEV-TEST-ANNOTATION-AUTO-FIX.story.md REQ-TEST-FIX-TEMPLATE REQ-TEST-FIX-PREFIX-FORMAT REQ-TEST-FIX-SAFE REQ-TEST-FIX-PRESERVE REQ-TEST-FIX-PLACEHOLDER REQ-TEST-FIX-NO-INFERENCE".
3) Helper implementation providing auto-fix logic - File: src/rules/helpers/require-test-traceability-helpers.ts
a) File-level @supports template insertion (REQ-TEST-FIX-TEMPLATE, REQ-TEST-FIX-PLACEHOLDER, REQ-TEST-FIX-SAFE, REQ-TEST-FIX-PRESERVE, REQ-TEST-FIX-NO-INFERENCE) - buildSupportsTemplateComment(customTemplate?: string): - Default baseTemplate: - "@supports docs/stories/XXX.X-STORY-NAME.story.md REQ-XXX-YYY REQ-XXX-ZZZ". - Emits a multi-line JSDoc-style comment: /** * @supports docs/stories/XXX.X-STORY-NAME.story.md REQ-XXX-YYY REQ-XXX-ZZZ * TODO: Replace the placeholder story path and REQ-IDs with real values for this test file. */ - Provides clear placeholders and explicit TODO guidance for developers. - Annotated with @supports for Story 021.0 and requirements REQ-TEST-FIX-TEMPLATE and REQ-TEST-FIX-PLACEHOLDER.
- insertSupportsTemplate(fixer, sourceCode, customTemplate?): - Determines insertIndex = 0, unless file starts with a shebang (#!), in which case it inserts immediately after the shebang line. - Calls fixer.insertTextBeforeRange([insertIndex, insertIndex], templateComment). - Ensures executable semantics and formatting are preserved; only comment text is added.
- ensureFileSupportsAnnotation(context, sourceCode, autoFixOptions): - fileComments = sourceCode.getAllComments(). - fileHasSupports = some comment with /@supports\b/. - If !fileHasSupports, context.report({ node: first comment or AST root, messageId: "missingFileSupports", fix: autoFixOptions.autoFixTestTemplate === false ? undefined : (fixer) => insertSupportsTemplate(fixer, sourceCode, autoFixOptions.testSupportsTemplate), }). - This only inserts a generic template; it never infers story paths or requirement IDs. - JSDoc ties this behavior to Story 021.0 requirements (including REQ-TEST-FIX-NO-INFERENCE).
b) Malformed [REQ-XXX] prefix normalization (REQ-TEST-FIX-PREFIX-FORMAT, REQ-TEST-FIX-SAFE, REQ-TEST-FIX-PRESERVE, REQ-TEST-FIX-NO-INFERENCE) - normalizeReqId(raw: string): - Trims and uppercases input; if it doesn’t start with "REQ" it’s returned unchanged (no guessing for non-REQ ids). - For strings starting with REQ: - Strips leading separators after "REQ": /^[-_\s:]+/. - Converts whitespace/underscores to dashes: /[\s_]+/g -> "-". - Collapses consecutive dashes: /-+/g -> "-". - Returns `REQ-${rest}` or "REQ-". - Ensures we normalize only existing IDs, never fabricate new requirement IDs.
- normalizeReqPrefixInDescription(description: string): string | null - Early exit if description already matches canonical form: /^\[REQ-[^\]]+]/. - Otherwise attempts two patterns at the start of the string: - Square brackets: /^\[\s*(REQ[^\]]*?)\s*](.*)$/i – normalizes inner REQ portion and rebuilds `[REQ-...]{rest}`. - Parentheses: /^\(\s*(REQ[^)]*?)\s*\)(.*)$/i – normalizes then converts to bracketed prefix. - Returns null if no recognizable REQ prefix; no auto-fix in that case.
- createUpdatedStringLiteralRaw(originalNode, newValue, sourceCode): - Reads raw text for literal; preserves original quote style (' " or `) and escapes internal characters. - Only changes the string value, leaving surrounding formatting intact.
- handleItOrTestCall(context, node, description, options): - Requires requireTestReqPrefix to be true; otherwise, exits early. - If description does not start with canonical [REQ-...]: - Computes normalizedDescription via normalizeReqPrefixInDescription when autoFixTestPrefixFormat !== false. - Always reports missingReqPrefix. - Adds a fix only if: - autoFixTestPrefixFormat !== false, - normalizedDescription !== null (i.e., recognizable REQ prefix), - first argument is a string Literal. - Fix uses fixer.replaceText(literalNode, createUpdatedStringLiteralRaw(...)). - If there is no recognizable REQ prefix at all (e.g., "missing prefix"), normalizedDescription is null, so no fix is attached—only a diagnostic—which enforces the story’s “no inference” rule.
- handleCallExpression(context, options): - Skips non-test call names; only acts on describe/it/test/context. - For describe, only validates story reference pattern; it does not change text or add story IDs. - For it/test, uses handleItOrTestCall as above.
Overall, helpers change only comments and string literals; they do not touch implementation code, satisfying the safety and preservation requirements.
4) Targeted tests for Story 021.0 - File: tests/rules/require-test-traceability.test.ts - Header: /** * Tests for: * - docs/stories/020.0-DEV-TEST-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION.story.md * - docs/stories/021.0-DEV-TEST-ANNOTATION-AUTO-FIX.story.md * @supports docs/stories/020.0-DEV-TEST-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION.story.md REQ-TEST-FILE-SUPPORTS REQ-TEST-DESCRIBE-STORY REQ-TEST-IT-REQ-PREFIX REQ-TEST-FRAMEWORK-COMPAT REQ-TEST-PATTERN-DETECT * @supports docs/stories/021.0-DEV-TEST-ANNOTATION-AUTO-FIX.story.md REQ-TEST-FIX-TEMPLATE REQ-TEST-FIX-PREFIX-FORMAT REQ-TEST-FIX-SAFE REQ-TEST-FIX-PRESERVE REQ-TEST-FIX-PLACEHOLDER REQ-TEST-FIX-NO-INFERENCE */
- Valid cases: - Confirms that a correctly formatted prefix `[REQ-TRACE-123]` is accepted and not modified, satisfying template/prefix preservation.
- Invalid cases for Story 021.0:
1) File-level template insertion (REQ-TEST-FIX-TEMPLATE, REQ-TEST-FIX-PLACEHOLDER, REQ-TEST-FIX-SAFE, REQ-TEST-FIX-NO-INFERENCE) - Input code without any @supports: - `describe('Story 020.0-DEV-TEST-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION', () => { it('[REQ-ONE] works', () => {}); });` - Expected output: - Adds exactly the placeholder block at top: /** * @supports docs/stories/XXX.X-STORY-NAME.story.md REQ-XXX-YYY REQ-XXX-ZZZ * TODO: Replace the placeholder story path and REQ-IDs with real values for this test file. */ followed by the original describe(...). - Confirms correct template content and position, and that only comments are added.
2) No inference when REQ prefix is missing (REQ-TEST-FIX-NO-INFERENCE) - Code includes @supports but it('missing prefix', ...) has no [REQ-...] prefix. - errors: [{ messageId: "missingReqPrefix" }]. - No output field: indicates that no fix is provided—matching the out-of-scope clause for inventing IDs.
3) Malformed prefix fixes (REQ-TEST-FIX-PREFIX-FORMAT, REQ-TEST-FIX-SAFE, REQ-TEST-FIX-PRESERVE) - Spacing: - Input: "[ REQ-TEST-FIX ] does something" -> Output: "[REQ-TEST-FIX] does something". - Underscore: - Input: "[REQ_TEST_FIX] does something" -> Output: "[REQ-TEST-FIX] does something". - Lowercase: - Input: "[req-lowercase] bad casing" -> Output: "[REQ-LOWERCASE] bad casing". - Parentheses: - Input: "(REQ-PAREN) with parens" -> Output: "[REQ-PAREN] with parens". - All are wired with errors: [{ messageId: "missingReqPrefix" }] and specific output strings, verifying behavior matches the story’s implementation notes.
5) Rule documentation (user-facing) for auto-fix behavior - File: user-docs/api-reference.md, section "traceability/require-test-traceability" - Description explicitly references Story 021.0 and explains: - Auto-fix can insert a safe, non-semantic file-level @supports placeholder template with TODO guidance. - Auto-fix can normalize malformed [REQ-XXX] prefixes that already contain a recognizable requirement ID, adjusting spacing, brackets vs. parentheses, underscores, and casing. - It never invents new requirement identifiers. - Options documented: - autoFixTestTemplate (default true). - autoFixTestPrefixFormat (default true). - testSupportsTemplate (template override for placeholder). - This satisfies the story’s Documentation acceptance criterion.
6) Full test suite execution - Command run: npm test -- --runInBand --verbose - Underlying runner: jest --ci --bail --runInBand --verbose - Output excerpt for the relevant test file: - PASS tests/rules/require-test-traceability.test.ts - All valid and invalid cases (including those tagged for 021.0) passed. - Overall Jest summary: - Test Suites: 1 skipped, 48 passed, 48 of 49 total - Tests: 2 skipped, 352 passed, 354 total - Confirms that the implementation and its tests are currently passing.
traceability.notes:
Based on the current code, tests, and documentation, Story 021.0-DEV-TEST-ANNOTATION-AUTO-FIX is fully implemented: - File-level @supports templates are automatically inserted for test files missing annotations, using a clear placeholder format and a TODO line. This is controlled via autoFixTestTemplate and testSupportsTemplate and is implemented in ensureFileSupportsAnnotation, with precise behavior validated by tests. - Malformed [REQ-XXX] prefixes in test names are normalized (spacing, underscores vs. hyphens, parentheses vs. brackets, casing) only when a recognizable REQ ID is already present. The logic is implemented via normalizeReqId, normalizeReqPrefixInDescription, and handleItOrTestCall, with multiple explicit test cases covering each malformed input form. - Safety and non-inference guarantees are respected: the rule never fabricates requirement IDs, never infers story paths, and only mutates comments and string literals, preserving test bodies and quote styles. Cases without any REQ prefix receive diagnostics but no auto-fix. - Integration with ESLint --fix is correct (meta.fixable: "code" and fixer callbacks registered conditionally) and verified via RuleTester tests that assert before/after output. - User documentation in user-docs/api-reference.md describes the new auto-fix behaviors and configuration options in line with the story’s requirements.
All acceptance criteria and listed requirements (REQ-TEST-FIX-TEMPLATE, REQ-TEST-FIX-PREFIX-FORMAT, REQ-TEST-FIX-SAFE, REQ-TEST-FIX-PRESERVE, REQ-TEST-FIX-PLACEHOLDER, REQ-TEST-FIX-NO-INFERENCE) are demonstrably satisfied and all associated tests pass. Status: PASSED.
